research_authorization: owner-authorized online research; BBROSE is open to new shapes/layouts/structures; research NOT limited to current BBROSE products; NO competitor product may be copied exactly
standing_rule: online measurements are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY unless manufacturer-authoritative; none of these values is a BBROSE specification until owner-confirmed

summary.note: no MANUFACTURER_TECHNICAL_DRAWING with full dimensioned tolerances was obtainable from public sources; supplier catalogues and retailer listings dominate

references.product_type: empty magnetic eyeshadow palettes, multiple pan counts
useful_structural_principles: a three-tier pan family (15 / 26 / 36 mm) covers eye, blush and face products
9-pan magnetic is the most common consumer format — a sensible pilot baseline
case material drives weight class, which drives perceived quality
must_not_be_copied: supplier's specific case styling or branding

references.source: Amazon listings — empty 26 mm magnetic pans (multiple vendors)
references.manufacturer_or_supplier: Allwon / Pangda and similar pan vendors
references.product_type: empty metal pans, round and square
useful_structural_principles: 26 mm is a genuine cross-vendor interchange standard — refill compatibility is a real design constraint
two depth families (3.5 and 5.0) exist at the same diameter; depth is an independent axis from diameter

references.source: Supplier catalogue dimensions aggregated via search (15-pan large format)
references.product_type: 15-pan large-format palette (12 x 1 g + 3 x 5 g)
useful_structural_principles: mixed-capacity layouts (small eye pans + larger face pans) are a mainstream format, not an exotic one
an 18 mm case height accommodates a deeper face pan alongside shallow eye pans
must_not_be_copied: the specific 12+3 arrangement as a signature layout

useful_structural_principles: a 150 x 90 case with 26 mm pans implies generous inter-pan spacing and margins — useful to bound the spacing range
case thickness can be as low as 15 mm for a single-level 26 mm/3.5 mm pan layout

references.source: Supplier catalogue — slim and ultra-slim formats
useful_structural_principles: 11.5-13 mm is the practical ULTRA-SLIM floor for a single-level palette
aspect ratio varies widely (78x85 near-square vs 134x67 elongated) — outer proportion is a free design variable
a square 83 x 83 x 12 case with a 3x3 grid implies ~26 mm pans on a ~27-28 mm pitch with small margins — a tight, efficient benchmark
must_not_be_copied: the exact outer square proportion as a BBROSE signature

useful_structural_principles: 30 mm pans exist alongside the 26 mm standard — pan diameter must be a parameter, never a constant
a 10 mm case is achievable when the lid carries no mirror
retail packs cluster 73-135 mm long, 60-74 mm deep, 12-20 mm thick
retailer dimensions often include outer packaging — treat as UPPER bounds, not case dimensions
must_not_be_copied: any brand's shade layout or graphic identity

references.source: Alovey — compact powder cases with mirror
useful_structural_principles: compacts pair an outer width with an inner godet diameter — the same two-level relationship palettes need (case vs pan)
58.5 mm is a recurring godet standard for face powder — the natural 'large face pan' anchor
closed thickness 14.5-19.5 mm for mirrored single-godet compacts; 31 mm for deep 11 g formats

references.source: Google Patents US20220408898A1 — refillable makeup palette with sliding drawer
references.product_type: refillable palette, sliding drawer, spring-tab pan retention

reported_dimensions.note: no dimensional tolerances stated; patent explicitly notes pressed-powder pans have WIDE size tolerance and the design absorbs it via spring pressure

useful_structural_principles: PAN TOLERANCE IS REAL: pressed-powder pans vary enough that retention must be compliant, not interference-fit — our pan-layout engine must carry a tolerance/clearance parameter
sandwiched retention (upward spring + downward frame) resists shipping movement
lid = hinged rear + clasp front + optional mirror is the canonical three-part architecture
must_not_be_copied: living-hinge removable compartment lids as claimed
angled rear stringer backstops as claimed

references.source: Google Patents EP0188547A1 — magnetic cosmetic case
references.product_type: magnetic pan retention with mirrored opposing section
useful_structural_principles: magnet-lined section + mirrored opposing section is long-established prior art — magnetic refill is a generic capability, not a novel claim to design around

references.source: Google Patents US5638838A — cosmetic compact snap-on hinge
useful_structural_principles: gudgeons + pivot pin + resilient snap jaws is the classic compact hinge family
the lid opens to a 'predetermined obtuse viewing angle' so the mirror faces the user — the open angle is a FUNCTIONAL requirement driven by mirror use, not a styling choice

references.source: Google Patents US20150201733A1 — portable interchangeable cosmetic compact
references.product_type: interchangeable tray locked into a base, clasped mirrored lids (clasps may be magnetic)
useful_structural_principles: a removable TRAY (not just removable pans) is a distinct refill strategy worth modelling as its own taxonomy axis
magnetic clasping is an alternative to mechanical clasping
must_not_be_copied: the claimed tray-locking and clasp arrangement

references.source: Injection-moulding design guidance (Protolabs, TDL, FOW and equivalents)
references.exact_or_analogous: ANALOGOUS (process guidance, not a product drawing)
useful_structural_principles: wall uniformity is a COSMETIC requirement (sink/warp), which makes it a visual-quality constraint, not only a manufacturing one
ribs stiffen tall lid walls instead of thickening them — relevant to thin palette lids
these ranges bound any plausible case wall we propose

references.source: Refillable magnetic palette vendors (Coosei, Make Up For Ever, Z Palette-class systems)
references.product_type: refillable magnetic palettes with mixed pan sizes

reported_dimensions.pan_equivalence_reported: blush ~= 3 eyeshadows; camouflage cream ~= 2 eyeshadows; brow powder ~= 1 eyeshadow
reported_dimensions.mixed_configurations: 4 small pans OR 1 large pan OR 1 medium + 2 small in the same zone

useful_structural_principles: mixed layouts can be EXPRESSED as module occupancy — but occupancy is a convenience for reflowable layouts, not a physical law; the engine must equally support direct dimension-based placement
must_not_be_copied: any vendor's specific case or insert design
references.owner_correction_2026_08_05: the blush~3 / cream~2 / brow=1 relationships are NOT a MANUFACTURER_STANDARD, INDUSTRY_STANDARD or PRODUCTION_RULE. They are a CALCULATED_LAYOUT_HEURISTIC only. Every module must resolve to explicit dimensions.

visual_references_note: R1, R5, R6, R7, R8, R15 also served as VISUAL_ANALOGUE material for proportion and format expectations; none was used to copy styling
gaps: no public MANUFACTURER_TECHNICAL_DRAWING with tolerances, draft angles or hinge pin dimensions was obtainable — supplier drawings are quote-gated
mirror thickness and mirror attachment method are not published in any source found
clasp force / detent specifications are not published
no source states a standard OPEN ANGLE in degrees; only 'predetermined obtuse angle' (R12)
pan tolerance is acknowledged as wide (R10) but never numerically specified
